issues with pattern: Red background with PREreview logo, large type reading Advisory Committee Meeting Minutes, and a meeting-date badge — all baked as a raster image. Post type and meeting date are structured data encoded as pixels: invisible to screen readers, untranslatable, unsearchable, and unfilterable. A freshly rendered image must be produced for every meeting just to change the date badge. Alt text that restates the visible text is required by WCAG but still blocks access to the date for screen reader users who already know the post type from context.
replaced by: postType: meeting-minutes + meetingDate: Date → header component renders the red band with logo and date badge in HTML/CSS; no image asset required; date is a machine-readable structured field

issues with pattern: Feature image is the PREreview wordmark on a red background and nothing else. Carries zero informational content — every post in this series has an identical or near-identical image. Wastes a Contentful asset slot and CDN bandwidth for every post. Alt text can only say PREreview logo which adds nothing a sighted user does not already know from being on the site. The image evolved through at least three naming generations (PREreview-Banner-640x240 / logo-horizontal-red-N / Product-weeknote-header) but remained semantically identical.
replaced by: postType: platform-news → renderer generates a consistent post-type label in HTML; no image asset required; the postType field also enables listing-page filtering by post type

issues with pattern: Older platform news posts (pre-October 2025) have no feature_image set and no body-level header image either. Inconsistent with the logo-only variant introduced later. When migrated to Contentful the rendered post has no header-level visual identity or type context at all.
replaced by: postType: platform-news → same renderer as the logo-only variant; consistently applied regardless of whether a header image was ever present; provides type context without requiring a new image asset

issues with pattern: A seasonal background photograph with a centred overlay box listing 3 topic bullets (A Sneak Peek at What's Inside). The bullet text — the actual table of contents for the newsletter — is baked as pixels over the photo. Inaccessible to screen readers, untranslatable, unsearchable. The background photograph is partially obscured by the overlay and has no alt text pathway. Requires producing a new rendered composite image for every newsletter edition.
replaced by: heroImage: Asset (the background photo alone) + newsletterPreviewItems: Symbol list of up to 3 items → newsletter header component overlays the bullet list from structured text fields; photo gets heroImageAlt

issues with pattern: A genuine editorial photograph (team photo; seasonal landscape; stock illustration of diversity/community) used as the newsletter header. This is the correct use of an image field — the image is purely visual and sets mood rather than encoding data. Issues: no alt text field exists on the current content type so alt text cannot be authored; the post-type context (that this is a newsletter) is not expressed in any structured field.
replaced by: heroImage: Asset + heroImageAlt: Symbol (required when heroImage set; empty string valid for decorative images) + postType: newsletter for type-level filtering and rendering context

issues with pattern: Older newsletters (2023 to early 2024) have neither a feature_image nor a header-level body image. Inconsistent presentation across the blog archive.
replaced by: postType: newsletter → renderer applies a newsletter header template without requiring a photo; heroImage remains optional for editions that have one

header pattern: Champion interview — per-person named branded header
issues with pattern: A template header image with the champion's name set in type over a branded background (e.g. Jade-blog-header.png / Alan-blog-header.png). The champion's name is baked as pixels: invisible to screen readers, unsearchable, and requires a freshly produced image for each interview. Older champion-authored essays (pre-2026) have no header at all, making the series visually inconsistent.
replaced by: postType: champion-interview → renderer reads the post title field and applies the branded interview header template in HTML/CSS; champion's name surfaces from structured content; no per-person image asset required

header pattern: Champions program — promotional and announcement images
issues with pattern: Heterogeneous group: some posts use branded template-style headers (Champions-blog-post-header-image-N.png); some use genuine editorial content (group photos, geographic distribution maps, bar charts) as the feature image; older posts (2024 and earlier) have no header at all. Editorial content that belongs in the body — e.g. a group photo of all champions — is being used as a header image, removing it from the richtext flow where it would have a caption and alt text.
replaced by: postType: champions-program for branded template headers → renderer generates consistent header; genuine editorial images (group photos / data charts) stay in richtext body with captions and alt text; heroImage optional for a single splash image with heroImageAlt

header pattern: Editorial series — named series branded header
issues with pattern: A per-series template header image encoding the series name in type (e.g. Special-blog-series-header---ASAPbio.png / FORCE11-Club-header.png / Instructional-Use-Design-Sprint-header.png). Series name is baked as pixels: not translatable, not machine-readable for filtering or navigation, and requires a new rendered image for each new series.
replaced by: postType: special-series + series: Symbol (e.g. ASAPbio Collaboration / Instructional Use Design Sprint) → renderer applies the series header template and surfaces the series name from a structured field; series field enables cross-series filtering and navigation

header pattern: Welcome post — generic reused stock photograph
issues with pattern: The same stock welcome photograph (a welcome sign or a welcome-on-board image) is reused unchanged for every new-hire announcement. The image carries no information about the specific person. The person's headshot — which does appear as the first body image in several of these posts — would be more informative and meaningful as the header.
replaced by: heroImage: Asset (person's headshot migrated from first body image where available) + heroImageAlt: Symbol naming the person

header pattern: Standalone blog post — thematic editorial photograph
issues with pattern: A genuine photograph relevant to the post topic (Portuguese tiles for a translation post; a waterfall for the from-surviving-to-thriving post; a sunset seascape for an annual reflection). Correct semantic use of an image header. Issues: no alt text field on the content type; several posts have no feature_image set and instead use the first body image as a de facto header — the image then appears twice, once at the top and once in the richtext body.
replaced by: heroImage: Asset + heroImageAlt: Symbol; migration should detect the first-body-image-as-header pattern (image appearing before any text block) and populate heroImage rather than leaving it in the richtext content field

header pattern: Standalone blog post — custom brand illustration
issues with pattern: PREreview-commissioned brand illustrations used as editorial feature images (PREreview_Illustrations_Illustration_B.png / _C.png). Correct semantic use. Issues: no alt text field; only two posts use this and neither has a consistent treatment.

header pattern: Ad-hoc editorial header — one-off branded graphic or screenshot
issues with pattern: Post-specific header images that do not fit any reusable template: strategic-plan feature images, a review-a-thon roadmap infographic, a product screenshot (homepage-splash.png), and a macOS screenshot (Screenshot-2025-09-03-at-8.53.47-AM.png). Screenshots used as hero images are particularly problematic — they contain UI text that screen readers cannot access, they age poorly as the UI changes, and they carry no alt text. The roadmap infographic encodes structured information (a roadmap timeline) as pixels.
replaced by: Evaluate per case: genuine thematic graphics → heroImage + heroImageAlt; UI screenshots → remove from header position and embed in body richtext with alt text describing the feature shown; roadmap infographic → keep as body image with descriptive alt text or consider a structured timeline content type

header pattern: No header image — general and legacy blog posts
issues with pattern: Posts from 2019–2023 covering platform announcements, journal club series, open reviewer pilots, COVID-19 rapid review, and early feature releases have no feature_image and no header-level body image. The majority of the blog archive falls into this group. No immediate a11y harm (absence of an image is not itself an accessibility failure) but presents an inconsistent reading experience and provides no post-type context.
replaced by: postType: blog-post → renderer degrades gracefully with no heroImage; for high-traffic legacy posts optionally backfill heroImage with a relevant photograph or illustration
